summary: Winfred Robert Martin (d. 1915) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and later as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Wing-tsit Chan (1901–1994) was a scholar in sinology and philosophy who studied at Harvard University (~1924–1929). He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1935–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

Winnifred Fallers Sullivan is a religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Cornell and the University of Chicago. She held academic posts at Washington and Lee, Chicago, University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington.
Winston Kyan is a scholar in sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under doctoral supervisor Hung Wu and teacher Linda Seidel.

Wm. Theodore de Bary (1919–2017) was a sinologist, philosopher, and Japanologist who studied at Columbia and Harvard. He served as Carpentier Professor of Oriental Studies at Columbia (1953–2017) and was president of the Association for Asian Studies (1969–1970).

Wolfgang Franke (1912–2007) was a sinologist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Hamburg. He held academic posts at Sichuan University and Peking University before serving as the sinology chair at Hamburg (~1950–1977).

Wolfgang Morgenroth (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Richard Hauschild at the University of Jena. He held academic appointments at Jena, the University of Greifswald, and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he was Professor of Indology.

Wolfgang Schultz (1881–1936) was a scholar of philosophy and history who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He managed the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and held the Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

Wolfgang Voigt (1911–1982) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar. He founded the Verzeichnis der Orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland and served as its General Editor from around 1957 to 1982.

Wolfram Eberhard (1909–1989) was a sinologist and historian who studied under Ferdinand Lessing in Berlin. He taught in China, served at Ankara University (1937–1948), and was Professor of Sociology at the University of California, Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Stony Brook University. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woosung Huh is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He served as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).
Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1985–1995) and held a post at the University of Amsterdam (~1999).
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Xi Cao is a scholar working in computational fields and Tibetology who has held posts at Minzu University of China and Tibet University.
Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Kelaniya and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong in 2016 under doctoral supervisor K. L. Dhammajoti.

Xianlin Ji (1911–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg. He had a long career at Peking University, serving as professor, vice president, and Life Professor.

Xiaoling Wu (1914–1995) was a scholar in sinology and Indology. He held appointments at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1947), Peking University (~1947–1952), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who was a doctoral student and postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).
Xiaoting Wei is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Cheng Mei Ku (attested 2004).
